texts.preamble: Koneti Kiran vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 20 October, 2022 Bench: A.Abhishek Reddy, Juvvadi Sridevi The Hon'Ble Sri Justice A.Abhishek Reddy And The Hon'Ble Smt Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Writ Petition No.32279 of 2022 Order:
texts.facts: The case of the petitioner is that basing on two (2) crimes viz., Crime Nos.300/2021 and 62/2022 of Manakondur Police Station and Chigurumamidi Police Station, respectively, the respondent No.2 passed the impugned detention order, dated 29.07.2022. According to respondent No.2, the detenu is a 'Goonda', as he has been habitually committing theft of cattle in the limits of Karimnagar Commissionerate, thereby creating large scale fear and panic among the general public, thus adversely affecting the public order, peace and tranquility in the area. Subsequently, the impugned detention order was confirmed by the Government vide G.O.Rt.No.1824, dated 23.09.2022. Though the first bail application filed by the petitioner in Crime No.62 of 2022 was dismissed by the learned Special Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Karimnagar, the second bail application is pending consideration. The impugned orders are legally unsustainable and ultimately, prayed to allow the Writ Petition, as prayed for. 5. Subsequently, the Government confirmed the impugned detention order vide G.O.Rt.No.1824, dated 23.09.2022. All the mandatory requirements were strictly followed by the detaining authority while passing the impugned detention order. The impugned orders are legally sustainable and ultimately, prayed to dismiss the Writ Petition.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that the impugned detention order has been passed in a mechanical manner and without application of mind. Therefore, the apprehension of the detaining authority that there is every likelihood of the detenu indulging in similar offences, which are prejudicial to the maintenance of public order, unless he is prevented from doing so by an order of detention, is highly misplaced. The alleged crimes do not add up to "disturbing the public order" and they are confined within the ambit and scope of the word "law and order". Since the offences alleged are under the Indian Penal Code, the detenu can certainly be tried and convicted under the penal code. Thus, there was no need for the detaining authority to invoke the draconian preventive detention law against the detenu. Hence, the impugned orders tantamount to colourable exercise of power. AAR,J & JS,J On the other hand, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents supported the impugned orders and submitted that the detenu is a 'Goonda'. He has been indulging in the theft of cattle, thus creating panic among the general public in the limits of Karimnagar Commissionerate and thereby acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order. Since the petitioner is still in judicial remand, the apprehension of the detaining authority that there is every likelihood of the detenu committing similar offences, is not misconceived. The series of crimes allegedly committed by the detenu were sufficient to cause a feeling of insecurity in the minds of the people at large. Therefore, the detaining authority was legally justified in passing the impugned detention order. In catena of cases, the Hon'ble Supreme Court had clearly opined that there is a vast difference between "law and order" and "public order". Hence, according to the Hon'ble Apex Court, the detaining authority should be wary of Koneti Kiran vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 20 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44045604/ 2 invoking the immense power under the Act. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar1, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has, in fact, deprecated the invoking of the preventive law in order to tackle a law and order problem. It was observed that every breach of public peace and every violation of law may create a 'law and order' problem, but does not necessarily create a problem of 'public order'. 9. In Kanu Biswas v. State of West Bengal2, the Hon'ble Apex Court, while discussing the meaning of word 'public order,' held that the question whether a man has only committed a breach of 'law and order' or has acted in a manner likely to cause a disturbance of the 'public order', is a question of degree and extent of the reach of the act upon the Society.
